messages:
maria_support: FYI — customer ACME hit a burst of 429s and then observed duplicate order creation when their client retried. They think our SDK defaults might be too aggressive. Escalating for engineering help.

maria_support: attaching the snippet they sent:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 3
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 24
{"error":"rate_limit"}
```

raj_engineering: thanks — do we know which SDK version they're on and whether they're sending an idempotency key for order creation? also did the client respect Retry-After or ignore it?

maria_support: they're on sdk-js v1.4.2, no idempotency key. here's the snippet of their client config they pasted:
```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({
  retry: { strategy: 'linear', attempts: 6, baseDelayMs: 200 },
});
client.createOrder(payload);
```
They say requests were concurrent from many users (50+ concurrent requests per sec), then many 429s, then retries that resulted in duplicate orders.

oliver_sdk: that config explains it — linear backoff + no jitter + 6 attempts is a recipe for synchronized retry spikes once quota resets. older SDK defaults we inherited were conservative for availability but bad for client-side herd.

oliver_sdk: immediate mitigations: 1) require customers to set an idempotency key for mutating endpoints (orders/payments). 2) have clients honor Retry-After header strictly. 3) switch to exponential backoff with full jitter for SDK defaults (e.g., expo base 100ms, max 5s, attempts 4).

raj_engineering: can you paste a minimal repro we can run locally to see the failure pattern? would like to replicate the quota-reset spike.

maria_support: customer repro (they used bash + curl):
```bash
# run 60 parallel create requests over 2s
for i in $(seq 1 60); do 
  curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/orders" "-H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' " "-H 'Content-Type: application/json' " "-d '{"item":"widget","qty":1}' &
done
wait
```
They reported many 429s then client retried and some requests succeeded twice (no idempotency token).

raj_engineering: perfect — I'll run that against a staging quota with our throttling. I want to capture the timings and whether Retry-After appears on all throttled responses. also checking whether our rate-limit headers are consistent across frontends.

oliver_sdk: temporary SDK patch customers can apply until we ship a default change:
```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({
  retry: {
    strategy: 'expo_jitter',
    attempts: 4,
    minDelayMs: 100,
    maxDelayMs: 5000
  },
  defaultIdempotency: true // injects idempotency-key header for create APIs
});
```
This reduces synchronized retries and prevents duplicates for most create flows. Also set the client to respect 429 Retry-After header and stop retrying beyond that window.

raj_engineering: server-side notes: we should ensure x-rate-limit-reset is precise (seconds till reset) and include Retry-After in 429 always. if frontends sometimes omit headers under overload that could break client heuristics. I'll add a check in the throttle middleware.

maria_support: I'm going to share the temporary patch and idempotency guidance with ACME now. they asked if duplicates imply billing issues — will escalate to billing if they confirm doubled charges.

incident-bot: Ticket #INC-2024-386 created: support->engineering escalation for 429 + duplicate-create repro. Link: https://tickets.redwood.ai/INC-2024-386

oliver_sdk: I'll open a PR to change sdk-js default retry strategy to expo_jitter + lower attempts and add a runtime warning when making mutating calls without an idempotency key. PR will reference this ticket.

raj_engineering: thanks — follow-ups for action items: (1) me: add server-side header consistency tests, (2) oliver: PR + changelog, (3) maria: send workaround + ask customer to confirm duplicates.

sara_cs: thanks all — sound plan. please ping me once ACME confirms billing impact so we can coordinate refunds if needed. :thumbsup:
